captions.linkedin:
Built an entire brand from nothing.

No brief. No identity. No product name. Just a dropship stainless steel cutting board sourced off a supplier page.

I named it KURA. Positioned it for home cooks who take kitchen hygiene seriously. Wrote the tagline ("Clean Surface. Clear Mind."), picked the palette (deep slate, warm cream, burnished copper), and built a three-font type system, display, serif, body, before writing a single line of HTML.

Then I built the homepage. It opens with a preloader that types the brand name in, then reveals: GSAP horizontal scroll on the use-case section, clip-path reveals on the brand imagery, a parallax hero, a marquee trust bar running on pure CSS, scroll-triggered fades on every section via IntersectionObserver. No external JS libraries.

The goal was never "nice website." It was making a product that costs $48 to source feel like it belongs next to brands spending millions on brand equity. That gap is design. It's copy. It's page speed. It's whether the above-the-fold gives someone a reason to keep reading.

Need a store like this built for your brand? That's what I do, DM me.
